Present Perfect Tense vs. Past Simple

You use the Present Perfect tense to talk about a finished action or event that is connected to the present in some way.

You use the Simple Past tense to talk about a finished action or event not necessarily connected to the present.

You can use the Present Perfect tense to talk about experience. When you use the Present Perfect tense, you think about the past and present together. There is some connection between what happened in the past and now.

For example:
I have learned English = I learned English in the past and now I can speak English.
He has bought a painting = He bought the painting in the past and now he has a painting.
Look at the chart about how to form the Present Perfect tense:
We use have/has + the past participle of the verb in Present Perfect sentences.

Find a list of verbs and their past participle forms. Memorize them.
I have always enjoyed sporting events.
I have had a lot of interesting experiences.
Would and used to have similar meanings. They are both used to describe something that happened regularly in the past but doesn't happen any longer.
My cousin and I would often go to football games.

However, there is an important difference between used to and would.

Would is not used unless you know that the time frame is in the past, while used to does not require this.

Read the following example:
We would visit India every summer when we were children.
When we were children refers to a past time frame and therefore makes the meaning of would clear.

We used to visit India every summer.
Here, you do not have to include a past time frame since the meaning of used to clear.
We would always buy a hotdog and can of soft drink at the game.
We used to sit near the edge of the field to soak up the atmosphere.

Write notes based on the answers.
Write an 80 to 100 word paragraph using the notes.  Use the Present Perfect tense and the Past tense.
Also, include a sentence with the words used to or would.
Read the paragraph aloud to the interviewee (the person you interviewed).

Write an 80 to100 word paragraph about a past experience related to sports and interests.
Use the Simple Past tense and Present Perfect tense.
     You use the Present Perfect tense to talk about a finished action or event that is connected to the present in some way.
     Example: I have gone to football games since I was a child.
     You use the Simple Past tense to talk about a finished action or event not necessarily connected to the present.
     Example: I caught the ball at the game.
You can also use the words used to and would to describe past habits.
     Example: I used to go to football games with my father.

images.text: When I was eleven years old, I stole a football.

I have always enjoyed sporting events. My cousin and I would often go to football games. We would always buy a hot dog and soft drink at the game. We used to sit near the edge of the field to soak up the atmosphere.
One day, my eyes were fixed on an extra ball on the sideline. I casually picked it up and walked out of the stadium.
As soon as I left, I was sorry. I noticed a huge guy standing nearby and thought he could be a policeman.
The powerful man came over to me. "Nice football," he said. I could have fainted.
I answered in a whisper, "Would you arrest me for something so small?"
The big man looked puzzled. "Why should I arrest you?"
"I stole this football," I said.
The man smiled. "I'm not a policeman," he said. "You could return the football if you wanted to."
"I can't," I said. "I would be in big trouble."

He took two steps forward and punted it. I couldn't believe my eyes.
"You could be a football player," I said, amazed.
"I am a football player," the big man said smiling. "And I think you might be one someday."
"Don't I wish," I said.
"I think I can take care of that," my new protector said. “I used to be just like you”.
That's the story of how I was "discovered" and how I have had a lot of interesting experiences. Ten years later, I became a star on the same football team. My nickname was "Stealer." No one but the coach knew why!
